Subject: Confidential: Manager kits & escalation matrix — 2026 review window

Team —

Attached are the draft manager kits and the initial escalation matrix for the 2026 annual review window. This packet is intended for people managers only (CONFIDENTIAL) — it contains sensitive guidance for handling reviews for privileged roles and ongoing performance-sensitive cases. Please do not forward outside the list.

Goals for this thread:
- Confirm the manager communication templates are appropriately de-escalatory for sensitive roles.
- Validate the escalation matrix (who to loop, timelines for legal/HQ intervention).
- Identify any missing sign-offs (legal/compliance).

Attachments: [Attachment: manager_kit_v1.docx (docx)], [Attachment: escalation_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx)], [Attachment: comms_snippets_v1.md (md)]

Key notes:
- Timeline: draft to be finalized by Friday, June 11th so we can publish manager kits the week of June 14th ahead of calibration.
- Silent-handling protocol needs explicit guidance: who gets notified, and whether the employee or manager is notified first.

Ask: please review and reply with lane-specific redlines or an explicit OK by EOD Wednesday (June 9th). If you suggest changes to the matrix, call out the row and the proposed replacement text.

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan
People Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

---
Note: docs are drafts for internal review only.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Confidential: Manager kits & escalation matrix — 2026 review window

Thanks Priya — quick read-through and a couple of notes:  

1) Escalation matrix: row for "suspected data-handling policy violation" currently routes to "People Ops" and "Legal" at the same time. Can we add a step to route first to Security (to preserve evidence) and then to Legal? I can map the suggested ordering (Security -> People Ops -> Legal) in the spreadsheet and send back.

2) Manager kit: the suggested wording for "documenting performance conversations" has a line that could be misinterpreted as creating a performance record accessible company-wide. Suggest adding a short blurb about privacy of manager notes and location (private HR folder vs manager notes).

I won't be able to do a deep edit today but I can take the escalation matrix and draft the modified ordering by tomorrow morning. If someone from Legal needs to pre-check the Security-first routing, please loop them.

- Marcus
Director, Engineering (applied infra)
Redwood Inference

Priya / Marcus —

Good points. I made two focused changes in the attached templates and a short addendum for managers who are handling sensitive roles:

- manager_email_templates_v2.docx: two tone options for initial and follow-up conversations (normal review vs sensitive-role review). The sensitive templates avoid language that implies disciplinary action and instead emphasize "next steps" and "support resources".
- silent_handling_protocol.pdf: a one-page decision tree that clarifies when to inform an employee vs when to pause communications while investigations occur.

For Marcus: I updated the escalation matrix to the Security -> People Ops -> Legal flow and added an explicit 24-hour response SLA for Security to acknowledge receipt.

Suggested edits for the manager kit: add a short paragraph under "Recording conversations" that reads: "Manager notes for development conversations should be written for coaching and stored in the manager's private HR folder. If notes include investigatory detail, consult People Ops before sharing."

Attaching: [Attachment: manager_email_templates_v2.docx (docx)], [Attachment: silent_handling_protocol.pdf (pdf)]

If Legal wants to comment, I'd prefer captured redlines in the doc rather than inline email comments. Priya — do you want me to route to CompLegal or do you want to loop our retained counsel?

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Head of Talent & Org Design
Redwood Inference
